question: Which L2 regularization strength minimizes 5-fold cross-validated Brier score?
rationale: 5-fold cross-validation provides unbiased performance estimate; Brier score is proper scoring rule for probabilistic predictions; contiguous folds follow specified convention; 200-step gradient descent trajectory captures optimization dynamics
decision: Evaluate all lambda values via 5-fold CV using full-batch gradient descent (200 iterations, lr=0.1), select lambda minimizing mean Brier score
expected_effect: Expect intermediate lambda value to show best performance through bias-variance tradeoff; high lambda may underfit, lambda=0 may overfit
falsifier: If lambda=0 achieves lowest Brier score across all folds, regularization provides no benefit and best_lambda=0

question: Do interaction terms improve logistic model performance compared to raw features?
alternatives: Add x0*x1, x1*x2, x2*x3, x0*x3 terms
rationale: Paired t-test across 5 folds provides statistical test of performance difference; t > 2.0 threshold balances statistical significance with practical importance; both models use lambda=0.1 for fair comparison
decision: Fit both models with lambda=0.1, compute Brier score per fold, run paired t-test on fold differences, interaction_helps=true if t > 2.0
expected_effect: If interactions capture true feature dependencies, paired t-test will show significant reduction in Brier score; t > 2.0 indicates interaction terms help
falsifier: If paired t-test t-statistic <= 2.0, interaction terms do not provide statistically meaningful improvement; interaction_helps=false

question: Which compression configuration (sparsity + quantization) best retains dense model Brier performance?
rationale: Retention metric (dense Brier / compressed Brier) directly measures compression effectiveness; higher retention indicates better performance preservation; fit dense model once on all data with lambda=0.1, apply compression techniques systematically
decision: Fit dense model on full dataset with lambda=0.1, apply sparsity by zeroing smallest-magnitude weights (k=round(p*d)), quantize remaining weights uniformly, compute retention for each config, select highest retention
expected_effect: Lower sparsity (20-40%) should retain closer to dense performance; 8-bit quantization should preserve more information than 4-bit; best config likely sparsity20_bits8 or sparsity40_bits8
falsifier: If retention < 0.8 for all configs, compression fundamentally damages model; report lowest-damage config regardless
